newsitem.title: POLAND: IMF TELLS POLAND TO ACT TO CURB C/A, TRADE GAP.
newsitem.headline: IMF TELLS POLAND TO ACT TO CURB C/A, TRADE GAP.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said Poland needed to make adjustments, such as balancing the budget and tightening its monetary policy, to keep its fast expanding current account and trade deficits in check.

"Domestic demand is still much larger than it should be and in effect both the trade and current account deficit are significantly larger than the most pessimistic forecasts from last year. This situation requires adjustments," IMF representative Markus Rodlauer told the Rzeczpospolita daily.
Rodlauer said the Polish government needed to show fiscal restraint and balance the budget by 1999 at the latest.

"We advise the government to do everything possible to limit the deficit already in 1997 and reduce it even further next year, so that producing a balanced budget is possible in 1999 at the latest," he said.
He said that Poland also needed to quickly tighten its monetary policy to slow domestic demand because fiscal policy was not elastic enough.
"There is a need for immediate action, we think it is necessary to tighten monetary policy as soon as possible."
He also said that even though wage growth has remained under control, there was a need to curb salary growth in inefficient public sectors such as mining.
Rodlauer said there was no need to devalue the zloty, but only if Poland implemented measures to curb internal demand.

"The IMF agrees with the majority in Poland's government that the zloty exchange rate is at a level where it can be sustained. However, this is subject to the conditiion that policies to slow domestic demand are implemented," he said.

In the first four months of 1997 Poland's C/A deficit widened to $2.3 billion, against a $1.4 billion shortfall in all of 1996. The trade deficit in the January-April period amounted to $4 billion, nearly half of the total 1996 gap.
